name: PostHog
summary: PostHog is an all-in-one product analytics tool that tracks page views and custom events, with session replay and error tracking built in.

free_plan_covers.note: The free plan includes 1,000,000 analytics events a month, plus 100,000 error tracking exceptions and 5,000 session recordings, enough for far more than 1,000 monthly visitors.

first_paid_usd_month.note: PostHog has no fixed-price monthly plan; past the free monthly allowance it charges pay-as-you-go per event with no cap, so cost depends on usage.

portability.note: PostHog's core product is open source under the MIT license and free to self-host with Docker Compose, so you are not locked into their cloud.

cookies.note: PostHog sets a cookie by default to recognize visitors, but it can be switched to cookieless_mode so it never sets one.

product_events.note: PostHog is built around custom event capture like posthog.capture(), not just automatic page views.

uptime_checks.note: PostHog's product lineup covers analytics, session replay and error tracking, but it does not check your site from outside or alert you when it goes down.

session_replay.note: PostHog can record what a visitor did on the page and play it back like a video, synced with console logs and network requests.

setup.step: Create a PostHog account, either PostHog Cloud or self-hosted.
Install the client SDK with npm install --save posthog-js.
Add your project token and host to .env.local and your hosting provider; find the token in your project settings.
Create instrumentation-client.js at your app root and call posthog.init() with those values; PostHog then captures page views automatically.

builder_notes: Keep personal details like emails and names out of event properties; identify logged-in users with a stable id such as their user id, and skip identify() entirely for anonymous visitors.
PostHog sets a cookie by default; if the app must run without cookies, initialize it with cookieless_mode instead of the default config.
